name: Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Soft Tissue Tumors Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of small round blue tumor cells arranged in alveolar pattern with fibrovascular septa
Positive staining for myogenic markers such as Myogenin and MyoD1
Detection of PAX3-FOXO1 or PAX7-FOXO1 gene fusion by molecular testing
Rapidly enlarging soft tissue mass in extremities or trunk

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with immunohistochemical positivity and detection of characteristic gene fusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular confirmation of PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion is critical for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging soft tissue mass with firm consistency
searchTerms: fast growing firm soft tissue lump

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of PAX3-FOXO1 or PAX7-FOXO1 gene fusion
searchTerms: presence of specific gene fusion in tumor

common.symptomName: Localized pain or tenderness at tumor site
Swelling causing functional impairment of affected limb
Constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms due to pulmonary metastases
searchTerms: respiratory symptoms due to lung spread

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to metastatic spread
searchTerms: brain or spinal symptoms from tumor spread

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal discomfort if primary tumor is retroperitoneal
searchTerms: belly discomfort due to tumor behind abdomen
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

rare.symptomName: Pathologic fractures due to bone invasion
searchTerms: fractures caused by cancer in bone
open wounds on skin above tumor

laboratory: Anemia of chronic disease in advanced cases
imaging: MRI showing soft tissue mass with heterogeneous enhancement
CT scan for detection of pulmonary metastases
other: Histopathology demonstrating alveolar architecture with fibrovascular septa
Immunohistochemical positivity for Myogenin and MyoD1

distinguishingFeatures: Embryonal subtype lacks characteristic PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion
Histology shows more primitive, less organized cells
EWSR1 gene rearrangement instead of PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion
Different histologic appearance with Homer Wright rosettes

redFlags: Rapid tumor growth with increasing size over weeks
Presence of distant metastases at diagnosis
Neurological symptoms indicating metastatic spread to CNS
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition, 2020
Molecular Pathology of Rhabdomyosarcoma, Pediatric Blood & Cancer, 2018
